title: Prepositions and Case Government
subtitle: On, fram, mid, tō — each takes its own case.
objectives: Understand and apply the concepts of Prepositions and Case Government.
Read and parse examples from authentic Old English texts.

sections.heading: Core concept
sections.body: Prepositions in Old English govern specific cases. Most take the dative. Some take the accusative when motion is involved. A few take the genitive. You must learn the case for each preposition. Common prepositions: on + dat/acc (on, in, onto), fram + dat (from), mid + dat/inst (with), tō + dat (to), þurh + acc (through), ofer + acc/dat (over).

sections.heading: Example
sections.body: On þǣm hūse (in the house, dat — location). On þæt hūs (onto the house, acc — motion).
